title: Breast Cancer Management
specialty: Medical Oncology, Breast Surgery and Radiation Oncology

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with early or locally advanced breast cancer: urgent referral, triple assessment and staging, receptor testing, MDT planning of surgery, systemic therapy and radiotherapy, endocrine therapy, bone protection and follow-up. Verified against NICE NG101 (updated 2025) and NICE NG12, with Saudi screening context from the PHA 2023 guideline; endocrine doses from FDA labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Saudi National Cancer Center breast guideline 2019 not accessible
Chemotherapy and targeted therapy doses not reproduced

pathophysiology.summary: Breast cancer is a group of epithelial cancers defined by oestrogen/progesterone receptor (ER/PR) and HER2 status. ER-positive tumours depend on oestrogen signalling; HER2-positive tumours on HER2 growth signalling; triple-negative tumours lack all three.
keyMechanisms: Receptor status drives treatment: endocrine therapy for ER-positive, anti-HER2 therapy for HER2-positive, chemotherapy for triple-negative.
Spread to axillary nodes is the main prognostic factor in early disease.
Distant spread to bone, liver, lung and brain.

symptoms: Breast lump, nipple change or discharge, skin change, axillary lump.
physicalSigns: Breast and axillary examination; skin tethering, peau d'orange.
redFlags: Unexplained lump 30 or over, or unilateral nipple change 50 or over — suspected cancer referral (NICE NG12 1.4.1)
Bone pain, breathlessness, neurological symptoms — metastatic work-up
precipitants: Oestrogen exposure (early menarche, late menopause, HRT)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma; imaging and biopsy.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: ER/PR positive; HER2 positive; triple negative.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer and diagnose
actions: Use NICE NG12 1.4.1–1.4.3 for urgent referral.
Triple assessment; axillary ultrasound; ER/PR/HER2 at diagnosis.

clinicalManagement.title: MDT plan
actions: Discuss all cases with receptor status available (NICE 1.3.5).
ER-positive: surgery plus systemic therapy rather than endocrine therapy alone unless unfit (NICE 1.4.1).
Neoadjuvant chemotherapy for HER2-positive or triple-negative disease where indicated (NICE 1.8–1.9); neoadjuvant endocrine therapy an option for postmenopausal ER-positive (NICE 1.11.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Adjuvant endocrine therapy
actions: Offer to all with ER-positive invasive cancer (NICE 1.11.6).
Postmenopausal, medium/high risk: aromatase inhibitor; low risk or AI intolerance: tamoxifen (NICE 1.11.8).
Premenopausal: shared decision on tamoxifen alone or with ovarian suppression, or ovarian suppression + AI (NICE 1.11.7).

clinicalManagement.title: Bone protection and radiotherapy
actions: Adjuvant bisphosphonate for postmenopausal node-positive disease; consider for high-risk node-negative (NICE 1.12.1–1.12.2).
Radiotherapy technique minimising heart and lung dose; breath-hold for left-sided (NICE 1.13.1).

learningObjectives: Diagnose, stage and plan treatment for early and locally advanced breast cancer.

keyPoints: AI for postmenopausal ER+ medium/high risk.
pitfalls: Endocrine therapy alone in fit women.
Forgetting bone health on aromatase inhibitors.

patientEducation: Side effects of endocrine therapy; adherence over years.
lifestyleAndDiet: Physical activity and healthy weight after treatment (NICE 1.16).
mdtReferrals: Breast MDT; genetics if family history; lymphoedema service.
dischargeCriteria: Written care plan with named MDT contact (NICE 1.15).
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Annual mammography for 5 years after treatment (not ipsilateral after mastectomy); no routine ultrasound or MRI surveillance (NICE 1.15.1–1.15.3).
